Gramlot 0.2.4 sandboxes an `iframe` whose `srcdoc` comes from Data, and repairs examples 10 and 13.

## What changes

- An `iframe` whose `srcdoc` comes from Data gets `sandbox=""`: its HTML is shown and runs nothing, no script, form, popup or access to the page. `srcdoc` comes from Data when it is a `^`/`=` pointer, a `==` expression, a `${…}` template reading a pointer, or when the node value is a pointer whose datum carries `srcdoc` in its `_wdg`. The Python and JavaScript renderers apply the same rule. Rules: [GC-090 §035](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/090-classes-and-hosts.md#gc-090-035), [GC-095 §065](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/095-writing-pages.md#gc-095-065).
- A literal `srcdoc` gets no `sandbox`. A `sandbox` written in the Source is kept as written.
- The live renderer writes `sandbox` before every other attribute of an element, so a change of `srcdoc` or `src` navigates with the current `sandbox`.
- Examples 10 (card removal) and 13 (live Source playground) use `connect_onclick`: since 0.2.3 their `onclick` stopped both pages at the first render.
- The core CI runs the browser checks of binding, strict CSP, `srcdoc` and examples 10 and 13 in Chromium.

## Upgrading from 0.2.3

- An `iframe` that must run the scripts of a `srcdoc` from Data declares its own `sandbox`, for example `sandbox='allow-scripts'`; the declared value turns the rule off.
- No other change for pages, in Python or JavaScript.
